issues.description: "After I go, my body feels great" uses bare "go" to mean "go to the gym". Out of context "after I go" means "after I leave", and the ellipsis is a poor model for A2 learners. It also weakens the after-clause demonstration.
issues.suggested_fix: Change to "After I exercise, my body feels great." (keeps the after clause, uses A2-level "exercise") or "After I go to the gym, my body feels great."

issues.description: The gloss for "body" ("your arms, legs, and head") omits the torso and could mislead a learner into thinking "body" means only the limbs and head.
issues.suggested_fix: Change the gloss to "all of you: your head, arms, legs and the rest" or "the whole physical person".

issues.description: The spec lists "week" as a review word, but it never appears in the script. "body" is recycled; "week" is not.
issues.suggested_fix: If the format allows, add a natural use of "week" (e.g. Anna: "I go to the gym three times a week, after work."), or accept the omission given the 10-15 second limit.

qa_report.summary: A clean, on-level micro dialogue: grammar is correct throughout and the before/after clauses are taught and modelled accurately ("after work" as a prepositional phrase alongside two genuine clauses is acceptable). One major collocation issue: "After I go, my body feels great" uses bare "go" where a native would say "after I exercise" or "after I go to the gym", and it muddies the grammar model. Minor issues: the "body" gloss is incomplete (omits the torso), and the review word "week" is not recycled. Fix the line s1l3 wording and the gloss, and this is ready to record.
